newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil mothers demand justice in castration cases.
newsitem.headline: Brazil mothers demand justice in castration cases.

text.p: The mothers of more than a dozen boys murdered and mutilated in one of Brazil's most macabre crime sprees appealed to Congress on Tuesday to help them in their long and fruitless battle for justice.

In a special hearing of the Chamber of Deputies' Human Rights Committee, the mothers from Altamira in the Amazonian state of Para called on the federal government to solve a 1989-1994 string of castrations and kidnappings.

Eight boys were murdered, four survived after having their testicles cut off, five are still missing and there were at least nine unsuccessful kidnapping attempts over four years, officials said. The crimes sparked fears of black magic sacrifices, an illegal international trade in genitals or a gang of psychotics prowling the Amazonian hinterland.

"We know we can never get our children back. But surely we can ask for justice," Rosa Maria da Silva Pessoa, president of the Committee in Defence of Children in Altamira and mother of one of the victims, told deputies.

Seven people were arrested in 1994 in connection with the castrations but the case has not progressed since then and most have been released for lack of evidence. The original police investigations in Para were so mishandled they led to accusations by victims' families and local media of an official conspiracy or, at the very least, involvement by police officers.

Federal government officials told the committee Para police failed to interview key witnesses, keep records of reported disappearances or ensure that their case against the principal suspects was legally watertight.
"They have been sleeping on the case. The years from the first crime to the last were four wasted years," said Humberto Pedrosa Espinola, a Ministry of Justice human rights official.

Two of the accused are doctors, two are former police officers and a fifth has been accused before of being a member of an international organ-trading ring. Witnesses claim one of the doctors took part in black magic ceremonies.

In a statement prepared for the hearing, the Committee in Defence of Children in Altamira said the victims were all male, aged between eight and 14 and from poor families. None of the severed sexual organs has ever been found.

The group, calling for Federal Police intervention, said the city was still in a "state of fear" because of the continued freedom of suspects and the certainty that more people were involved. "The passage of time will not have helped the investigators because clues have gone missing, memories are fading and the likelihood of impunity has become ever stronger," it said.
